newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela inflation falls to 2.6 pct in January. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT 1/2]
newsitem.headline: Venezuela inflation falls to 2.6 pct in January. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT 1/2]

text.p: Venezuela's inflation rate in January was 2.6 percent, down from 8.1 percent in January 1996 (Corrects from "down from 3.0 percent in January 1995") and 3.0 percent in December 1996, the central bank said.

January's rate brought inflation over the past 12 months to 92.9 percent, compared with 64.2 percent in the 12 months to January 1995. In 1996, inflation reached 103.2 percent -- the highest rate in Latin America.
The January drop extends a decline that began after the prices blipped higher in October because of utility price increases.

Monthly inflation peaked at 12.6 percent last May. It has fallen since then thanks to the April launch of an economic reform program supported by the International Monetary Fund. The plan removed currency and interest rate controls and increased gasoline prices fivefold.

Government officials have said they see inflation for the coming year at about 25 percent. Analysts see inflation closer to 35 percent, citing wage claim pressure and further utility price increases in the pipeline.

The central bank said January's monthly rate was boosted by a 3.8 percent rise in prices for foods, drinks and tobacco. "This was principally because of heavy rains, which affected harvesting thus reduced offer of agricultural goods," it said.
Prices for shoes and clothing rose just 0.2 percent, "which is explained by falling demand and high supply, characteristic of this time of year," the bank said.
Household expenses -- "affected by telephone tariff increases" -- rose 2.7 percent, and the category of "various expenses" rose 2.1 percent.
